headline: Hills between you and the nearest masts are the likely cause [los_ee][los_o2][los_three][los_vodafone][network_comparison].
explanation: The ground rises above the direct line to every identified mobile mast site, so your signal is likely weakened rather than completely lost. O2's site is the least obstructed, with terrain 129 m above the line 985 m away [los_o2][network_comparison]. All identified sites are 3.8–5.7 km away [nearest_site][los_vodafone][los_ee][los_three][los_o2], which can also weaken signal . There are no speed tests recorded near your address this quarter, so we cannot confirm current speeds from measurements [speed_cell][speed_neighbours]. A Met Office yellow wind warning is in force with gusts up to 74.9 km/h and heavy rain [weather][met_office_warnings], which may cause temporary degradation now but does not explain a persistent problem [weather].

rule_based.rule: Operators ranked by line of sight from this point to their nearest identified site (clear, then marginal, then blocked); clear lines by distance, obstructed ones by how far the ground rises above the line.
rule_based.text: No operator has a clear line of sight to an identified site from here. Least obstructed: O2, a site 5.7 km south-east (inferred from crowd-sourced data), with terrain 129 m above the line.

limitations: Sites are approximate and operator names are inferred from crowd-sourced data, so distances and margins are uncertain; antenna heights are assumed; Ofcom figures are area-level predictions, not exact for this address [nearest_site][operators_5km][los_ee][los_o2][los_three][los_vodafone][ofcom_area].
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.

critiques.reason: All four line-of-sight checks show terrain rising 129–288 m above the direct line to the nearest identified sites, with assumed 25 m antenna heights. Even allowing for higher antennas, the obstructions are substantial. The evidence is strong and consistent.
The nearest site is 3.8 km away and all operator sites lie 3.8–5.7 km distant. Crowd-sourced positions add uncertainty, which the belief acknowledges, so the confidence is appropriate.

Only 3 operators (EE, Three and Vodafone) have approximate mast sites within 5 km [operators_5km]. Operators are inferred from crowd-sourced data [operators_5km]. The belief correctly states a single-operator gap is not proven and assigns a low confidence.

The weather evidence is live (forecast and warning) and can only explain a recent drop. Without speed trend data we cannot tell whether poor service is persistent (which would downgrade weather's role) or only recent (which would support it).
